countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.
countries.metaTitle: Study in India: Guide for International Students
countries.metaDescription: Regulators, admission routes, entrance tests, student visa and FRRO rules that international applicants should verify before applying to an Indian university.

universities.name: JSS Academy of Higher Education & Research
universities.summary: JSS Academy of Higher Education & Research is a private deemed-to-be university in Mysuru, Karnataka, formerly JSS University, focused on the health sciences. It runs JSS Medical College, JSS Dental College & Hospital and JSS College of Pharmacy in Mysuru, a second pharmacy college in Ooty, Tamil Nadu, and departments of allied health, life sciences, public health and health system management.
universities.campusLifestyle: The main campus at Sri Shivarathreeshwara Nagara, Mysuru 570015 holds the medical, dental and pharmacy colleges, with more than 650 faculty teaching about 3,500 undergraduates, 2,500 postgraduates and 700 research scholars. The university reports over 800 international students from more than 35 countries. Campus facilities listed for international students include a primary health centre, pharmacy, library, gymnasium, indoor and outdoor sports, food courts, a bank branch and ATM, NRI apartments, Wi-Fi and in-campus cycle services. Clinical teaching is linked to the 1,800-bed JSS Hospital in Mysuru.
universities.cityProfile: Mysuru is a heritage city in southern Karnataka, about 175 km by road from Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru, which is the usual arrival airport for international students. The airport Flybus runs directly to Mysuru in about four hours for roughly INR 800, the Shatabdi Express covers Bengaluru to Mysuru by rail in about two hours, and buses from Bengaluru's Satellite Bus Stop leave about every ten minutes for INR 180 to 300. JSS AHER's medical, dental and pharmacy colleges and most departments are in Mysuru, but JSS College of Pharmacy, Ooty is an off-campus college in Udhagamandalam in the Nilgiris district of Tamil Nadu, so the campus named on an offer letter decides where the student lives.
universities.practicalExposure: Practical training is organised by college. Pharmacy students at the Mysuru and Ooty colleges follow the Pharmacy Council of India B.Pharm syllabus, with a Practice School in the seventh semester and industrial training at a pharmaceutical company. Medical Laboratory Technology students train in the laboratories of JSS Medical College and hospital across biochemistry, microbiology, pathology and blood bank, handling automated analysers, histopathology processing and blood-component preparation, then complete a twelve-month internship. The MBA in Hospital Administration uses the 1,800-bed JSS Hospital for hospital postings in the third and fourth semesters, followed by an eight-week internship and a project. The M.Sc Nutrition and Dietetics programme includes a hospital and community nutrition internship in the third semester and a dissertation in the fourth. JSS AHER's placement cell and international students cell support students across these colleges.
universities.hostelOverview: JSS Medical College runs separate hostels for men and women with furnished rooms, a pantry and laundry in each block, RO drinking water and hostel kitchens, plus separate postgraduate hostels outside the campus. JSS College of Pharmacy, Mysuru has its own hostels for men and women. The 2026 hostel fee published for medical and dental entrants at JSS Medical College is INR 1,68,100 a year for men and INR 1,64,500 for women, paid at reporting and separate from tuition. NRI apartments are listed among campus facilities. Hostel places are applied for on the university's prescribed form.
universities.dietarySupport: Hostel kitchens serve residents in each JSS hostel block, and the Mysuru campus has canteens, restaurants, a cafeteria and food courts for students and visiting parents. A bank branch, ATM, post office and healthcare clinic are on campus, so day-to-day money and health needs can be handled without leaving. JSS AHER advises international students to take out health insurance on arrival and to bring prescriptions for any regular medicines.
universities.safetyOverview: JSS Medical College hostels have round-the-clock male and female security guards for the respective hostels and CCTV monitoring, and the campus has a 24-hour security service. An anti-ragging cell operates on campus. The Student Support Centre, run with the departments of psychiatry and clinical psychology, offers free and confidential counselling for stress, anxiety, depression and adjustment to a new environment.
universities.studentSupport: The International Students Cell, chaired by the Dean (Academics), is the single window for foreign applicants: it issues the provisional admission letter used for the visa, guides airport transfers, collects registration and tuition fees on arrival, and provides the bonafide letter for e-FRRO registration and later visa extensions. Contact: international@jssuni.edu.in or +91 98455 55625.
whyChoose: NRI and Foreign National fees are published in US dollars for 2026-27, from USD 2,500 for the M.Sc Nutrition and Dietetics to USD 6,000 first-year tuition for the B.Pharm, so the programme cost is known before applying.
The B.Pharm is offered at two constituent colleges, Mysuru and Ooty, both on the NBA's accredited Pharmacy UG register, and placed 7th and 4th in the NIRF 2025 Pharmacy rankings.
JSS AHER holds NAAC A++ accreditation with a CGPA of 3.61 in Cycle 3, declared in October 2024, and ranked 21st in the NIRF 2025 University category.
Health-sciences teaching sits beside the 1,800-bed JSS Hospital, which the MBA in Hospital Administration and the allied health programmes use for postings and internships.
A dedicated International Students Cell issues the provisional admission letter for the visa and assists with airport transfer, fee collection and FRRO registration.
thingsToConsider: MBBS and BDS are not open through the international cell: both run on NEET-UG and Medical Counselling Committee deemed-university counselling, and JSS AHER's 2026 BDS fee notice lists all 100 seats as All India management seats with no NRI category.
SAARC-country students on the BBA and MBA programmes are billed in rupees on the Indian fee schedule rather than the US-dollar NRI/Foreign schedule, so fee comparisons differ by nationality.
Several fee schedules state only the first-year figure, and the pharmacy schedule adds other fees that are not given in US dollars, so the full-course cost is not published in one document.
B.Pharm applicants sit a JSS AHER online entrance test (23 June 2026 in the last cycle), while allied health, MBA and M.Sc seats are allotted on qualifying marks subject to an interview.
The application fee must be paid online by card, UPI or internet banking, and several brochures refer to debit cards issued in India, which can complicate payment from abroad.
Start dates differ widely: pharmacy classes began in early July, while allied health, MBA and M.Sc sessions began between September and October in recent cycles.
bestFitFor: Pharmacy applicants from Africa, South Asia or the Middle East who want an English-taught B.Pharm with a US-dollar fee and a choice between a city campus and a hill-station college.
Nepali B.Pharm applicants who can combine admission with the Embassy of India COMPEX scholarship route listed by JSS AHER.
Graduates from any discipline aiming for hospital or health-system management roles, through an MBA taught beside a teaching hospital.
Science school-leavers with Physics, Chemistry and Biology who want a laboratory-medicine degree with a full year of internship built in.
Science graduates who want a clinical and community nutrition master's with hospital internship at a moderate US-dollar fee.

faq.question: Is JSS Academy of Higher Education & Research a public or a private university?
faq.answer: It is a private, self-financing deemed-to-be university. The UGC lists JSS Academy of Higher Education and Research, Mysore among institutions declared Deemed to be Universities, with effect from 28 May 2008, and it was previously known as JSS University. It is not a state or central government university: fees are set by JSS AHER and published separately for the Merit category and for NRI and Foreign National students.

faq.question: Who counts as an international applicant at JSS AHER?
faq.answer: JSS AHER recognises three international categories. Foreign Nationals hold a foreign passport. PIO applicants hold a PIO card and are citizens of another country. NRI applicants took the 10+2 or bachelor's qualifying examination outside India. Allied health, MBA and M.Sc programmes reserve 15 per cent of seats for NRI and Foreign National candidates; the B.Pharm reserves 15 per cent for the NRI, Foreign and Management category.

faq.question: What is the language of instruction, and is IELTS or TOEFL required?
faq.answer: JSS AHER's regulations for the B.Pharm, the allied health B.Sc programmes, the MBA in Hospital Administration and the Faculty of Life Sciences M.Sc programmes all state that teaching and examinations are in English. The 2026 admission brochures do not list an IELTS or TOEFL score among required documents. For the B.Pharm and the allied health degrees, English must be one of the subjects in the qualifying school examination.

faq.question: Can I enter directly with a foreign school-leaving or bachelor's qualification?
faq.answer: Yes, where it matches the programme's subject and mark rules. The allied health brochure accepts 10+2 or equivalent from India or abroad after 12 years of study, with at least 50 per cent across Physics, Chemistry and Biology. For the B.Pharm, a foreign qualification must be recognised by the Association of Indian Universities as equivalent to 10+2. Foreign nationals applying to allied health and M.Sc programmes also need an eligibility certificate issued by JSS AHER.

faq.question: Is there an entrance test or interview?
faq.answer: It depends on the programme. B.Pharm selection uses qualifying-examination marks and a JSS AHER online entrance test at 10+2 level in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics or Biology; in 2026 the test was held on 23 June. For B.Sc Medical Laboratory Technology, the MBA in Hospital Administration and the M.Sc Nutrition and Dietetics, seats are allotted on qualifying marks subject to passing an interview.

faq.question: What does a programme cost an international student?
faq.answer: The 2026-27 NRI and Foreign National fees are: B.Pharm USD 6,000 first-year tuition plus other fees; B.Sc Medical Laboratory Technology USD 3,500 for the first year; MBA in Hospital Administration USD 5,200 a year, USD 10,400 in total; M.Sc Nutrition and Dietetics in Mysuru USD 2,500 for the first year. Hostel is extra: JSS Medical College's 2026 hostel fee is INR 1,68,100 a year for men and INR 1,64,500 for women.

faq.question: How do I apply?
faq.answer: Applications are made only online through the JSS AHER admissions portal: register, choose the programme, upload mark sheets, passport and photographs, and pay the application fee online. JSS AHER checks eligibility and sends a provisional admission letter with fee details, which is used for the student visa. After the visa is issued and the fee paid, the student reports to Mysuru or Ooty for final admission. JSS AHER states that it has no agents.

faq.question: What visa do I need, and what happens after arrival?
faq.answer: Foreign nationals need an Indian student visa endorsed to JSS AHER, applied for with the provisional admission letter; nationals of Nepal and Bhutan do not need a visa, and PIO and OCI holders do not need a student visa. Registration on the e-FRRO portal is required within 14 days of arrival. India's Study in India guidance requires a Ministry of Health No Objection Certificate for medical or paramedical courses.

faq.question: When do courses start and when should I apply?
faq.answer: Pharmacy runs earliest: in 2026, applications closed on 15 June, the entrance test was on 23 June and classes were set to begin on 10 July. Allied health, MBA and M.Sc applications opened in mid-February 2026. In recent cycles the allied health session began on 23 September 2025, the MBA on 9 October 2025 and the two-year M.Sc Life Sciences on 9 September 2024.

faq.question: Are scholarships available for international students?
faq.answer: JSS AHER's international students cell lists external schemes rather than an institutional waiver: the Government of India Study in India programme, through which JSS AHER states it has granted full scholarships; the Embassy of India COMPEX scheme for Nepali students taking B.Pharm; Royal Government of Bhutan scholarships; the Ministry of External Affairs scheme for Syrian nationals; and the e-VBAB programme for African students.

faq.question: What do JSS AHER's accreditations and rankings mean for my home country?
faq.answer: NAAC's A++ grade with a CGPA of 3.61 (Cycle 3, declared October 2024), the NBA accreditation of the B.Pharm at both pharmacy colleges and the NIRF 2025 rankings are Indian quality-assurance and ranking outcomes. They do not by themselves license a graduate to practise abroad; pharmacist, laboratory or dietitian registration depends on the rules of the regulator in the country where the graduate plans to work.

faq.question: Where will I live, and what does accommodation cost?
faq.answer: Students apply for hostel places on JSS AHER's prescribed form. JSS Medical College has separate men's and women's hostels with furnished rooms, pantries, laundry and security, plus postgraduate hostels outside the campus; the pharmacy college in Mysuru has its own hostels, and NRI apartments are listed among campus facilities. The 2026 JSS Medical College hostel fee is INR 1,68,100 a year for men and INR 1,64,500 for women.

faq.question: Should I choose the B.Pharm at Mysuru or at Ooty?
faq.answer: The syllabus, entrance test, 100-seat intake and USD 6,000 first-year NRI/Foreign tuition are the same at both colleges. The differences are location and ratings: Mysuru is on the main university campus, while Ooty is a hill town in Tamil Nadu. NBA accreditation for the B.Pharm runs to 30 June 2028 at Mysuru and 30 June 2027 at Ooty, and NIRF 2025 placed Ooty 4th and Mysuru 7th in Pharmacy.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
evidence.internalNotes: The qualifying-exam basis has changed between cycles (SAT in earlier cycles, JEE Main for 2026-27). Never state the accepted exam without naming the admission year. Corroborated by dasanit.org, which describes DASA as an MoE scheme for Foreign Nationals, PIOs, OCIs and NRIs to NITs, CFTIs and other premier technical institutions other than IITs.

evidence.claimText: Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and Foreign Nationals are eligible to appear in NEET (UG) and are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges subject to the rules of the respective State Governments, institutions and the Government of India. Foreign applicants must upload documentary proof of nationality with the application and are directed to confirm eligibility with the competent state and counselling authorities.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, National Testing Agency
evidence.internalNotes: Chapter 6, sections 1-2. No India medical page may present a NEET-free route. Eligibility is explicitly conditional on state and institution rules, so it varies by college.

evidence.claimText: The National Assessment and Accreditation Council, established in 1994 as an autonomous institution of the UGC, assesses and accredits Indian higher education institutions.
